title: Chemistry
description: Elements, the periodic table, bonds, acids and reactions.

questions.text: What is the chemical formula of water?
questions.explanation: A water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

questions.text: The atomic number of an element is the number of:
questions.explanation: The number of protons defines the element; protons plus neutrons is the mass number.

questions.text: What is the pH of pure water at 25 °C?
questions.explanation: Pure water is neutral, with pH 7.

questions.text: Which gas makes up most of the Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.

questions.text: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
questions.explanation: Na comes from the Latin name 'natrium'; S is sulfur.

questions.text: What is the chemical formula of table salt?
questions.explanation: Table salt is sodium chloride.

questions.text: Which of these is a noble gas?
questions.explanation: Neon is in group 18 with helium, argon, krypton, xenon and radon.

questions.text: What is the approximate value of the Avogadro constant (per mole)?
questions.explanation: One mole contains about 6.022 × 10²³ particles.

questions.text: A bond in which atoms share electrons is called:
questions.explanation: Covalent bonds share electron pairs; ionic bonds transfer electrons.

questions.text: A solution with a pH below 7 is:
questions.explanation: Below 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral, above 7 is basic.

questions.text: Which is the lightest element?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen has one proton and is the lightest element.

questions.text: What is the approximate molar mass of CO₂?
questions.explanation: 12 (carbon) + 2 × 16 (oxygen) = 44 g/mol.

questions.text: Which gas is produced when zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂.

questions.text: What are the horizontal rows of the periodic table called?
questions.explanation: Rows are periods; columns are groups (also called families).

questions.text: Which element has the symbol Fe?
questions.explanation: Fe comes from the Latin 'ferrum'; fluorine is F and lead is Pb.

questions.text: What does a catalyst do?
choices: Speeds up a reaction without being used up
Is a reactant that is always used up
questions.explanation: A catalyst lowers the activation energy and is left unchanged at the end.

questions.text: What is the change from solid directly to gas called?
questions.explanation: Dry ice (solid CO₂) sublimes without becoming liquid.

questions.text: Isotopes of the same element differ in their number of:
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same protons but different neutrons, so different mass numbers.

questions.text: What is the reaction between an acid and a base called?
questions.explanation: Acid + base → salt + water.

questions.text: What is the electric charge of a proton?
questions.explanation: Every proton carries one positive elementary charge.
